lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex! I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Is Alex living with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask a couple of follow-up questions.

Do you contribute towards the cost of supporting Alex (for example, by paying towards his food, clothing, or other living expenses) for at least the same amount as the current Child Benefit rate?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help support him. I send money regularly for his clothes, food, and things he needs for school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

One more important question: Is Alex's mum (or anyone else) already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Are you and Alex both currently living in the United Kingdom?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - I'm living abroad at the moment. Alex is in the UK with his mum, but I'm not there right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's important information.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation abroad? Specifically:

1. Which country are you currently living in?
2. Are you working while abroad, and if so, is it for a UK-based employer or are you employed locally in that country?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain. I'm working for a local Spanish company over here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more question about your situation:

Are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas), or is your time in Spain a permanent move, or is it temporary?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a permanent move - I relocated here for work and I'm settled in Spain now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all of this information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Residency Requirement:** To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to be living in the United Kingdom. While there are some exceptions (such as for Crown servants posted overseas, temporary absences, or those working abroad for a UK-based employer), your situation doesn't fall into any of these categories since you have permanently relocated to Spain and are working for a local Spanish company.

**Alternative Option:** Since Alex lives in the UK with his mum, she may be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him instead. It might be worth suggesting she look into making a claim, as she appears to meet the basic eligibility criteria of being responsible for a child and living in the UK.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
